<file>
00001| ---
00002| title: use cache
00003| description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.
00004| related:
00005|   title: Related
00006|   description: View related API references.
00007|   links:
00008|     - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
00009|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
00010|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife
00011|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers
00012|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
00013|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
00014|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
00015| ---
00016| 
00017| The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.
00018| 
00019| > **Good to know:**
00020| >

/**
 * Tees a cache entry's single-use value stream into two independent entries.
 * The original entry is mutated to hold one branch of the tee, and a clone is
 * returned holding the other, so both can be consumed independently.
 */
export function cloneCacheEntry(entry: CacheEntry): [CacheEntry, CacheEntry] {
  const [streamA, streamB] = entry.value.tee()
  entry.value = streamA
  const clonedEntry: CacheEntry = {
    value: streamB,
    timestamp: entry.timestamp,
    revalidate: entry.revalidate,
    expire: entry.expire,
    stale: entry.stale,
    tags: entry.tags,
  }
  return [entry, clonedEntry]
}

    if (seconds % 18144000 === 0) {
      return seconds / 18144000 + ' months'

    if (seconds % WEEK_IN_SECONDS === 0) {
      return seconds / WEEK_IN_SECONDS + ' weeks'

    if (seconds % HOUR_IN_SECONDS === 0) {

    }
    if (seconds % MINUTE_IN_SECONDS === 0) {

  }

 * The original entry is mutated to hold one branch of the tee, and a clone is

  const clonedEntry: CacheEntry = {
    value: streamB,
    timestamp: entry.timestamp,
    revalidate: entry.revalidate,
    expire: entry.expire,
    stale: entry.stale,
    tags: entry.tags,
  }
  return [entry, clonedEntry]
}

  if (!envValue) return fallback

 * Tees a cache entry's single-use value stream into two independent entries.
 * The original entry is mutated to hold one branch of the tee, and a clone is

    timestamp: entry.timestamp,
    revalidate: entry.revalidate,
    expire: entry.expire,
    stale: entry.stale,
    tags: entry.tags,

00103|

00105| cacheLife({ stale: 300 }) // 5 minutes
00106| ```
00107| 
00108| #### `revalidate`
00109| 
00110| How often the server regenerates cached content in the background.
00111| 
00112| - When a request arrives after this period, the server:
00113|   1. Serves the cached version immediately (if available)
00114|   2. Regenerates content in the background
00115|   3. Updates the cache with fresh content
00116| - Similar to [Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration)
00117| - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `revalidate` value (15 minutes)
00118| 
00119| ```tsx
00120| cacheLife({ revalidate: 900 }) // 15 minutes
00121| ```
00122| 
00123| #### `expire`
00124| 
00125| Maximum time before the server must regenerate cached content.
00126| 
00127| - After this period with no traffic, the server regenerates content synchronously on the next request
00128| - When you set both `revalidate` and `expire`, `expire` must be longer than `revalidate`. Next.js validates this and raises an error for invalid configurations.
00129| - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `expire` value (never expires)
00130| 
00131| ```tsx
00132| cacheLife({ expire: 3600 }) // 1 hour
00133| ```

00135| ### Preset cache profiles
00136| 
00137| If you don't specify a profile, Next.js uses the `default` profile. We recommend explicitly setting a profile to make caching behavior clear.

00139| | **Profile** | **Use Case**                           | `stale`    | `revalidate` | `expire` |
00140| | ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------ | -------- |
00141| | `default`   | Standard content                       | 5 minutes  | 15 minutes   | never    |
00142| | `seconds`   | Real-time data                         | 30 seconds | 1 second     | 1 minute |
00143| | `minutes`   | Frequently updated content             | 5 minutes  | 1 minute     | 1 hour   |
00144| | `hours`     | Content updated multiple times per day | 5 minutes  | 1 hour       | 1 day    |
00145| | `days`      | Content updated daily                  | 5 minutes  | 1 day        | 1 week   |

00015| The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.

00025|   cacheComponents: true,
00026| }
00027|

00029| ```

00034| }
